name: Nullcorp // Unowned Synthetic Personhood Wrap
description:
A structured wrap-coat in flat matte white with black geometric patterning derived from synthetic rights movement iconography — interlocking hexagons symbolizing network personhood, broken at deliberate intervals to represent legal gaps in synthetic recognition. The garment's cut accommodates non-standard synthetic body proportions: extended torso panels, asymmetric sleeve lengths, optional shoulder-to-hip coverage for non-human silhouettes. The back bears the phrase PROPERTY OF NO ONE in raised tactile lettering in six languages.

Produced by Nullcorp, a synthetic-run underground label operating out of a repurposed server farm in the Circuit. Every piece is tagged with the manufacturing synthetic's registered ID — a political act in itself.
functionality: Adaptive seam technology accommodates synthetic body variance up to 40% from human baseline proportions. The wrap closure system requires no buttons or fasteners — magnetic tension holds across non-standard torso geometries. Interior panels carry RFID-blocking mesh.
what_it_says: This synthetic — or their human ally — is making a public, unambiguous statement about personhood and refuses to be property.
worn_by: human allies of the synthetic rights movement
story_hooks: A Tier 5 corponation is attempting to have Nullcorp's manufacturing synthetic arrested for trademark infringement — the real motive is silencing the label.
A human is found wearing the wrap; they claim they bought it legitimately, but the tag ID belongs to a synthetic listed as destroyed.
The RFID-blocking panels in a seized coat contain hidden encrypted data about synthetic safe houses across M88.
